REGARDING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential for acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community service is at the forefront when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The aforementioned efforts are carried out with the aim of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional territory, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 10

(1) Other violence as referred to in article 4 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.

(2) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.

(3) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where someone/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 1

Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic, social exploitation, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. 13. a. Non-physical sexual harassment is an act directed at the body, sexual desire, and/or reproductive organs with the intention of degrading the dignity and honor of a person based on their sexuality and/or decency.

Types of non-physical violent behavior include dominant behavior from one party that is controlling, degrading, intimidating, insulting and harassing both verbally such as speech and non-verbally such as attitude.

b. Physical sexual harassment is any person who commits physical sexual acts directed at the body, sexual desire, and/or reproductive organs with the intention of degrading the dignity and honor of a person based on their sexuality and/or decency

REGARDING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential for acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community service is at the forefront when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The aforementioned efforts are carried out with the aim of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional territory, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 15

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and community as referred to in Article 14 letter b and letter c, shall be carried out in the form of participation of the private sector and community.

(2) Forms of participation of the private sector and community as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. preventing acts of violence against women and children; b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of violence. (3) Forms of participation of the private sector and community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER III

WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 8

Neglect as referred to in Article 4 letter d includes: a. acts of intentionally neglecting women within her household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or due to consent or agreement he is obligated to provide livelihood and care to that woman.

b. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children in a proper manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;

c. acts of intentionally neglecting to care for or attend to children as they should be, committed by parents, guardians, or any other parties responsible for their care.

(3) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where someone/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic, social exploitation, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. 13. Violence against women and children in the household is any act against a woman and child that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, economically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household sphere. Article 7

a. Non-physical sexual harassment is an act directed at the body, sexual desire, and/or reproductive organs with the intention of degrading the dignity and honor of a person based on their sexuality and/or decency.

Types of non-physical violent behavior include dominant behavior from one party that is controlling, degrading, intimidating, insulting and harassing both verbally such as speech and non-verbally such as attitude.

b. Physical sexual harassment is any person who commits physical sexual acts directed at the body, sexual desire, and/or reproductive organs with the intention of degrading the dignity and honor of a person based on their sexuality and/or decency

Physical sexual harassment includes unwanted touching, leading to sexual acts such as kissing, patting, pinching, glancing or staring lustfully. c. Sufficiently clear.

d. Sufficiently Clear.

h. Sexual slavery is any person who unlawfully places a person under their power or another person's power and renders them powerless with the intention of sexually exploiting them

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential for acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community service is at the forefront when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The aforementioned efforts are carried out with the aim of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional territory, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic, social exploitation, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. 13. Violence against women and children in the household is any act against a woman and child that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, economically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household sphere. 14. Human Trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, falsification, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 15. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb. 16. Woman is a person (human) who has genital organs, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed. 18. PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential for acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community service is at the forefront when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The aforementioned efforts are carried out with the aim of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional territory, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 7

a. Non-physical sexual harassment is an act directed at the body, sexual desire, and/or reproductive organs with the intention of degrading the dignity and honor of a person based on their sexuality and/or decency.

REGARDING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential for acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community service is at the forefront when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The aforementioned efforts are carried out with the aim of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional territory, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 25

(1) The Regional Government shall establish partnerships with the business world in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(2) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through: a. notification of job opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;

b. education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.

c. Development of facilities and infrastructure related to the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential for acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Community service is at the forefront when there is potential for violence against children. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential for acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community service is at the forefront when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The aforementioned efforts are carried out with the aim of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional territory, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 15

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and community as referred to in Article 14 letter b and letter c, shall be carried out in the form of participation of the private sector and community.

(2) Forms of participation of the private sector and community as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. preventing acts of violence against women and children; b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of violence. (3) Forms of participation of the private sector and community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 16

The obligations of families and/or parents as referred to in Article 14 letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 5

Physical violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a constitutes acts that result in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causing death of women and/or children.

Article 6

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 4 letter b constitutes acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

CHAPTER III

FORMS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST

WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 10

(1) Other violence as referred to in article 4 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.

(2) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.

(3) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where someone/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 8

Neglect as referred to in Article 4 letter d includes: a. acts of intentionally neglecting women within her household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or due to consent or agreement he is obligated to provide livelihood and care to that woman.

b. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children in a proper manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;

c. acts of intentionally neglecting to care for or attend to children as they should be, committed by parents, guardians, or any other parties responsible for their care.

REGARDING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential for acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community service is at the forefront when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The aforementioned efforts are carried out with the aim of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional territory, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

REGARDING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential for acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community service is at the forefront when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The aforementioned efforts are carried out with the aim of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional territory, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Parents are biological father and/or mother, or father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. LEGAL SECTION SETDA PESISIR BARAT REGENCY

26. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upwards or downwards and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of the woman and/or child. 27. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 28. Child-Friendly Regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of the government, community, business world and media that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children. 29. Private Sector is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media.

Article 25

(1) The Regional Government shall establish partnerships with the business world in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(2) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through: a. notification of job opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;

b. education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.

c. Development of facilities and infrastructure related to the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

Article 5

Physical violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a constitutes acts that result in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causing death of women and/or children.

Article 6

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 4 letter b constitutes acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

Article 15

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and community as referred to in Article 14 letter b and letter c, shall be carried out in the form of participation of the private sector and community.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF WEST PESISIR REGENCY

NUMBER 6 OF 2022

REGARDING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential for acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community service is at the forefront when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The aforementioned efforts are carried out with the aim of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional territory, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Region is Pesisir Barat Regency. 3. Regional Government is the administration of Governmental Affairs by the Regional Government and Regional House of Representatives based on the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the State of the Republic of Indonesia. REGARDING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential for acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community service is at the forefront when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The aforementioned efforts are carried out with the aim of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional territory, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 25

(1) The Regional Government shall establish partnerships with the business world in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(2) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through: a. notification of job opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;

b. education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.

c. Development of facilities and infrastructure related to the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and community as referred to in Article 14 letter b and letter c, shall be carried out in the form of participation of the private sector and community.

(2) Forms of participation of the private sector and community as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. preventing acts of violence against women and children; b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of violence. (3) Forms of participation of the private sector and community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 16

The obligations of families and/or parents as referred to in Article 14 letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

REGARDING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential for acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community service is at the forefront when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The aforementioned efforts are carried out with the aim of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional territory, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.
